# Start with looking at trends of Age and Weight
ggplot(AbaloneData, aes(x = Age, y = Weight, color = Sex)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE) +
  labs(x = "Age", y = "Weight", title = "Relationship Between Abalone Age and Weight")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

ggplot(AbaloneData, aes(Weight, Age, color = Sex)) +
     geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
     geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
     facet_wrap(~ Sex) +
     labs(title = "Age vs Weight by Sex")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

#Lets test it:
model <- lm(Weight ~ Age, data = AbaloneData)
summary(model)

library(GGally)
library(ggplot2)

GGally::ggpairs(
  AbaloneData,
  columns = c("Age", "Diameter", "Length", "Height",
              "Weight", "Shucked.Weight", "Viscera.Weight", "Shell.Weight"),
  aes(color = Sex, alpha = 0.7)
)

num_vars <- c("Age", "Diameter", "Length", "Height",
              "Weight", "Shucked.Weight", "Viscera.Weight", "Shell.Weight")

abalone_M <- subset(AbaloneData, Sex == "M")[, num_vars]
abalone_F <- subset(AbaloneData, Sex == "F")[, num_vars]
abalone_I <- subset(AbaloneData, Sex == "I")[, num_vars]

cor_M <- cor(abalone_M, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
cor_F <- cor(abalone_F, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
cor_I <- cor(abalone_I, use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

ggcorrplot(cor_M, lab = TRUE, title = "Correlation Matrix — Males")

ggcorrplot(cor_F, lab = TRUE, title = "Correlation Matrix — Females")

ggcorrplot(cor_I, lab = TRUE, title = "Correlation Matrix — Infants")

#----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#Now that we know our data, lets do our prediction model with the data set

AbaloneData$Sex <- as.factor(AbaloneData$Sex)

model <- lm(Age ~ Sex + Diameter + Length + Height +
              Weight + Shucked.Weight + Viscera.Weight + Shell.Weight,
            data = AbaloneData)

#Provides the best return
model_simpler <- lm(Age ~ Sex + Height + Weight +
                     Shucked.Weight + Viscera.Weight + Shell.Weight +
                     Sex:Height + Sex:Weight + Sex:Shucked.Weight +
                     Sex:Viscera.Weight,
                   data = AbaloneData)



full_mod <- lm(Age ~ Sex + Height + Weight + Diameter + Length +
                 Shucked.Weight + Viscera.Weight + Shell.Weight +
                 Sex:Height + Sex:Weight + Sex:Shucked.Weight +
                 Sex:Viscera.Weight,
               data = AbaloneData)

model_stepAIC <- step(full_mod, direction = "both", trace = FALSE)
summary(model_stepAIC)

full_model <- lm(Age ~ Sex * (Height + Weight + Length +
                                 Shucked.Weight + Viscera.Weight +
                                 Shell.Weight),
                data = AbaloneData)

best_model <- step(full_model, direction = "both", trace = FALSE)

summary(best_model)

#We need to run best model on the test data where we get judged on how accurately we predict

# Load in the data set we will use to predict attrition for the competition
CompData = read.csv(file.choose(),header = TRUE)

# Predict class labels
CompData$Predicted_Age <- predict(best_model, CompData)

# Write to CSV to submit in project
write.csv(CompData, "PredictionsBailey_Age.csv", row.names = FALSE)
